conditions: I-DR-BE-001: Remove or replace the 'field_present' helper reference in the §5 pseudocode (the function does NOT exist in the validator; only 'in fm' is used). Either (a) replace pseudocode 'field_present(fm, field)' with 'field in fm' to match the actual codebase idiom; or (b) declare 'field_present' as a NEW helper to be introduced by the extension. The current text implies it is pre-existing, which is a fabricated-API risk per KB-general-coding-principles Dimension 4.

I-DR-BE-002: Correct the codebase citation that 'field_present exists in the existing file per VE-002 and lines 145-155'. VE-002 documents make_finding only; lines 145-155 contain the closing portion of parse_frontmatter (not field_present). Either remove the line citation or replace with an accurate one.
verdict.rationale: Gate 0 passes cleanly. Gate 1 quality is strong overall — consistency with PRD/synthesis/codebase-analysis is high, NFR-8 backward-compatibility treatment is rigorous (pre/post empirical regression corpus baseline-capture procedure is explicit and well-grounded), the 4th-category dispatch decision is well-rationalized against two rejected alternatives, EARS ACs are testable. Two narrow but concrete issues attach to a single illustrative code block in §5 (fabricated/misattributed helper reference). Neither blocks acceptance — the validator dispatch design is correct independent of the helper-name choice — but they should be corrected before lock so plan-author and the implementer do not import the fabricated reference into the implementation step. No critical issues; no Gate 1 score below 80.

issues.location: backend-design.md §5 — pseudocode at lines 130 and 147 (calls `field_present(fm, field)` and treats it as pre-existing)
issues.description: The pseudocode in §5 calls `field_present(fm, field)` as if it were an existing helper in `validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py`. Verification against the actual file shows no such function exists. The validator uses bare `in` checks throughout (e.g., line 315: `if status == "superseded" and "superseded_by" not in fm`). The design's §5 explanatory footnote also claims 'field_present exists in the existing file per VE-002 and lines 145-155' — but VE-002 is the make_finding shape (not field_present), and lines 145-155 contain the tail of parse_frontmatter.
issues.evidence: grep -n 'def ' .claude/skills/auditing-shared/scripts/validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py returns only: parse_frontmatter, doc_type_category, make_finding, validate_agent_frontmatter, validate_pipeline_artifact, validate_skill_frontmatter, validate_file, parse_args, main. No field_present.
issues.why_important: KB-general-coding-principles Dimension 4 (no fabricated APIs) — even in an 'illustrative' sample, a helper named as if it exists in the project sets up the implementer to import a non-existent dependency. The footnote acknowledges this is illustrative pseudocode but explicitly justifies it by claiming the helper exists, which is incorrect.
issues.suggestion: Either (a) replace `field_present(fm, field)` with `field in fm` (the actual idiom — keeps the sample faithful to the existing validator and removes the fabricated reference), OR (b) declare `field_present` as a NEW helper this extension introduces and add a one-line note in §5 stating 'helper introduced by this extension' (legitimate if there is a compelling reason, e.g., distinguishing presence-with-empty-value from absence). Option (a) is recommended — the existing validator gets along without such a helper.

issues.location: backend-design.md §5 (footnote after pseudocode, around line 158): 'no fabricated APIs — `make_finding` and `field_present` exist in the existing file per VE-002 and lines 145-155'
issues.description: Even if I-DR-BE-001 is resolved via Option (a) and the field_present reference is removed, the citation linking 'lines 145-155' to a helper-existence claim should be corrected. VE-002 (in codebase-analysis.json) documents only the make_finding shape at validator lines 157-167. Lines 145-155 of the validator are the tail of parse_frontmatter, not a helper definition site.
issues.evidence: Read of validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py lines 144-167: line 144 is the closing of parse_frontmatter; lines 147-154 are doc_type_category; lines 157-167 are make_finding (matches VE-002).
issues.suggestion: Update the footnote citation to: 'no fabricated APIs — `make_finding` exists per VE-002 at lines 157-167; companion-field presence is checked with `in fm` per the existing pattern at lines 314-323 (the superseded_by enforcement)'.

issues.description: §7 specifies the regression-corpus layers (L1/L2/L3/L4) and the pre/post diff procedure, satisfying the reviewer's 'Output comparison defined when design replaces/modifies existing behavior' check. However, the corpus enumeration commits to '27 files minimum' for L2 and '27 synthetic fixtures minimum' for L3 without specifying how the count is verified — and Q-BE-5 explicitly defers the L2 storage decision (checked-in vs. snapshot-of-findings-only) to composer + plan-author. If composer adopts Q-BE-5 Option (c) (findings-only snapshot), the L2 fixture count is moot — what matters is the findings-JSON shape. This is consistent and not a defect, but plan-author and test-acceptance-author may benefit from a one-line note in §7 reconciling 'minimum 27 L2 files' with the Q-BE-5 Option (c) alternative.
issues.evidence: §7 L2 row: '27 files minimum'; §16 Q-BE-5: 'capture findings JSON only (not the source files)'.
issues.suggestion: Add a one-line note to §7's L2 row: 'If Q-BE-5 Option (c) is adopted (findings-JSON snapshot), the 27-file minimum applies only to the corpus the snapshot was captured against; the artifact-of-record becomes the findings JSON, not the source files.' This avoids implementer confusion at plan-execution time.

issues.description: The design cites the validator as '422 lines' (§2) but the actual file is 421 lines as of HEAD cf48e5e. The 'lines 365-371' citation for the outer dispatch is correct. The 'lines 314-323' citation for the ADR-0005 superseded_by enforcement is correct. The 'lines 145-155' citation (see I-DR-BE-002) is incorrect. These minor drifts do not affect the design's correctness but are worth tightening.
issues.evidence: wc -l validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py → 421. Line 365-371 contains the dispatch (verified). Line 314-323 contains the superseded_by enforcement (verified). Line 145-155 does NOT contain a helper definition (verified).
issues.suggestion: Replace '422-line file' with '421-line file as of cf48e5e' (or remove the line count, which is not load-bearing). Other line citations: verify lines 314-323 (correct), 365-371 (correct), 157-167 for make_finding (per VE-002).

issues.location: backend-design.md §2 paragraph 'One new branch inside `validate_pipeline_artifact` that delegates ... Branch order: GATED → ANALYSIS → ADR → ISSUE → unknown'
issues.description: The current validator's dispatch inside validate_pipeline_artifact does not use a sequential elif chain at the same level — it uses `doc_type_category(doc_type)` returning one of {'gated', 'adr', 'analysis', 'unknown'} and then branches on the returned category. The cleanest extension is to add 'issue' as a fourth return value of doc_type_category (when doc_type ∈ ISSUE_DOC_TYPES), then add a fourth `elif category == 'issue'` branch inside validate_pipeline_artifact. The design's 'Branch order' phrasing is consistent with this mechanism but reads as if a new elif chain is being introduced. A one-line clarification would tighten alignment with the existing mechanism.
issues.evidence: validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py lines 147-154 (doc_type_category function); lines 274-312 (validate_pipeline_artifact uses category branching).
issues.suggestion: Refine §2 item 4 to: 'One new branch inside `validate_pipeline_artifact` keyed on `category == "issue"` (where `doc_type_category` is extended to return "issue" when `doc_type ∈ ISSUE_DOC_TYPES`). Branch evaluation order parallels the existing gated/adr/analysis branches.'

issues.description: Verification Strategy quality check: §7 defines correctness ('diff baseline.json post-extension.json must be empty'), verification method (pre/post diff on L1+L2+L4), and timing (immediately after implementation). However, the 'early verification point' — the smallest concrete first target to validate the design — is not named explicitly. A natural early-verification target would be: 'Add ISSUE_DOC_TYPES + ISSUE_STATES constants only (no validate_issue_artifact yet); run the existing test corpus and confirm zero changes; this verifies the doc_type_category extension does not accidentally re-classify any existing doc_type.' Naming this would close the reviewer's 'Early verification point identifies a concrete first target' check.
issues.evidence: §7 specifies 4 steps (baseline / implement / re-run / diff) but does not decompose 'Implement extension' into a smallest-first-target sub-step.
issues.suggestion: Add a one-bullet 'Early verification target' note to §7 between steps 1 and 2: 'Step 1.5 (smallest first commit): Add the three new constants only (ISSUE_DOC_TYPES, ISSUE_STATES, ISSUE_PER_STATE_REQUIRED_FIELDS) and extend doc_type_category to return "issue" when doc_type ∈ ISSUE_DOC_TYPES. Re-run validator against L1+L2 corpus; diff against baseline; expect empty. This isolates the doc_type_category extension from the validate_issue_artifact function and surfaces any accidental re-classification of existing doc_types in the smallest possible diff.'

summary: Backend Design for issue-capture-mechanism-r1 — narrow scope (single Python script extension), high blast radius (NFR-8 backward compatibility). Gate 0 passes cleanly. Gate 1 quality is strong: D-10 (validator extension) rationale matches synthesis recommendation and codebase-analysis evidence; existing 21-value doc_type enum and 3 per-category state vocabularies preserved untouched (verified by reading validate_pipeline_frontmatter.py lines 38-68); NFR-8 backward-compat addressed both structurally (additive 4th branch) and empirically (pre/post regression diff with explicit L1+L2+L3+L4 corpus layers); EARS ACs (AC-BE-1..AC-BE-9) are testable; dependencies on design-cc explicitly named in both prose and companion JSON. Two recommended-severity corrections relate to a single illustrative code block in §5 (a helper named as if pre-existing — field_present — does not exist in the validator). Four additional polish recommendations. No critical issues; no blocking issues. Verdict: PASS_WITH_RECOMMENDATIONS — approved with conditions to clear before Blueprint composition lock.
